Priya — attaching the first batch and answering the bullets inline below. Attaching: redwood_saml_metadata.xml, scim_provisioning_log_excerpt.csv, rbac_matrix.xlsx, mfa_policy.pdf

SAML / SSO:
- Protocol: SAML 2.0 supported. Both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows are supported; we accept standard AuthnRequests and respond with signed assertions.
- Metadata: see attached redwood_saml_metadata.xml (entityID: https://api.redwood.ai/saml, ACS: https://console.redwood.ai/saml/acs).
- Single logout: supported when configured by customer IdP.

SCIM provisioning:
- Protocol: SCIM 2.0 (JSON over HTTPS) with bearer token.
- Deprovisioning: we perform soft-deletes for 30 days by default (configurable per tenant) then hard-delete on retention expiry.
- Deduplication: provisioning calls match by externalId and primary_email; if both conflict we open a human-review ticket (see control narrative).
- Evidence: scim_provisioning_log_excerpt.csv (rows show create, update, deactivate events; timestamps are UTC).

RBAC / least-privilege:
- Roles: we publish a default role set (Owner, Admin, Developer, Billing, ReadOnly). The attached rbac_matrix.xlsx maps API scopes and Console actions to roles.
- Least-privilege: new user defaults to ReadOnly; privilege elevation requires Admin approval (console workflow + audit trail). We use role-scoped tokens for service accounts; no user credentials are embedded in automation.

MFA:
- Enforcement: MFA is enforced for all interactive console logins for tenant admins and developers by policy. Supported factors: TOTP (authenticator apps), WebAuthn (hardware keys).
- Evidence: mfa_policy.pdf summarizes enforcement and configurable exceptions (exceptions require risk-based justification and Security Ops approval).

Notes: API keys and long-lived tokens are exempt from interactive MFA but are covered by separate key rotation and usage monitoring controls.

Let me know if you want raw log slices or screenshots; we can redact PII and share via the Drive link.

- Dev
